Bianca: Hey Kristi! How was the workshop?
Kristi: It was good but I realize how much work has to be done. My résumé has to be tailored to each job I apply to and more action words are needed. The résumé isn't the only place where more work is needed.
Bianca: What do you mean?

Kristi: A cover letter where a concise introduction is composed is crucial. They emphasized, when I did the workshop, that every cover letter must be sent with a résumé. Your cover letter should explain how the work experience listed on your résumé will make you a good candidate for the position or the company.
Bianca: Your cover letter is the document where you give a more personal introduction to yourself. So were the suggestions that were given at the workshop pertinent to writing a cover letter?

Kristi: Yes. We were given the fundamentals. The time when you draft a cover letter is the time to think about specific components. First, the letter should have four paragraphs. The first paragraph should state where you found the job lead and that you are applying for a particular job. If there is a job title or job posting number, you should include that as well. The second paragraph is a short profile which highlights your skills, experiences and achievements. The third paragraph states clearly how your specific abilities and skill sets would be valuable to the company and position. The fourth paragraph closes the letter. You should thank the company for their time and for reviewing your résumé. You should also say that you will follow up with a short call.
Bianca: Wow, there's a lot to include!
Kristi: And you also need to remember to research the company so you can address the letter to a specific person, including their title.

Subject and Object Relative Clauses to Express Time and Place

When you want to clarify which person or thing you are talking about, you use a relative clause. You use relative clauses to give more information about the person, place or thing you are talking about. They are used to make sentences more complex.

You can begin a relative clause with who for people, which for things or that for either people or things.
You can begin a relative clause with when for time and where for place.
You put the relative clause immediately after the noun it talks about.
A subject relative clause describes the subject of the clause and comes after the subject of the sentence.
An object relative clause describes the object of the clause and comes after the object of the sentence.
Relative Adverbs
Relative adverbs are used like relative pronouns:

When = is used for a time: The time when I went to the workshop.
Where = is used for a place: The workshop where I learned about cover letters.

It was emphasized when I did the workshop.
(It was emphasized then.)

The cover letter is where you give a more personal introduction.
(You give a more personal introduction there.)

The résumé isn't the only place where more work is needed.
The cover letter is the document where you give a more personal introduction.
A cover letter where a concise introduction is composed is crucial.
The emphasis, when I did the workshop, was on how a cover letter must be sent with a résumé.
The time when you draft a cover letter is the time to think about specific components.
How to Write a Cover Letter

A cover letter must be sent with your résumé when you apply for a job.
Below are some tips on how to write a great cover letter.
What goes into a good cover letter:

• The Meet and Greet (first paragraph)
    Open by stating where or how you got the job lead, then say that you would like to apply for the job. If there is a job title or job posting number, you should include that as well. Give details on your skill sets, focusing on how they would qualify you for consideration. This will signal that you pay attention to details, and are professional. Be mindful of the language you use. It should demonstrate how well you write and communicate.

  • Your Skills and Experience (second and third paragraphs)
    Outline your skill sets, areas of expertise, and accomplishments that might be of interest to your prospective employer.

  • Getting the Interview (fourth paragraph)
    Explain as concisely as possible how you could be valuable both to the company and to the position. Demonstrate that you have researched the company by showing how what you have to offer is a strong match to the job description. Your goal is to make the company want to call you in for an interview.
Guidelines for Your Cover Letter

• Write one concise page
  • After you write the first draft, revise and edit it
  • To itemize skill sets, accomplishments, and job experience, use bullet points
  • Simple formatting is always best
  • Use a basic font like Arial or Verdana
  • Find someone who can read through your cover letter and help you edit it before sending it
A cover letter must be sent with a résumé.
The letter should have four paragraphs.
The first paragraph should state where you found the job lead and that you are applying for a particular job.
The second paragraph is a short profile which highlights your skills, experiences and achievements.
The third paragraph states clearly how your specific abilities and skill sets would be valuable to the company and position.
The fourth paragraph closes the letter.
You also need to remember to research the company so you can address the letter to a specific person, including their title.
